title: Data-driven discovery of dynamical models in biology
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00955-4

This Technical Review compares data-driven approaches for discovering dynamical models in biology, focusing on regression-based methods, network-based architectures and decomposition techniques. It describes how these approaches extract dynamical information from time-resolved data and evaluates their strengths, limitations and complementarity.

title: Radioactive molecules as laboratories of fundamental physics
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00950-9

Radioactive molecules containing octupole-deformed nuclei offer a promising platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics. This Perspective discusses how advances in their production, trapping and molecular quantum control are enabling precision tests of fundamental physics at energy scales complementary to those probed by high-energy colliders.

title: Electrospray ion beam deposition for scanning tunnelling microscopy of complex molecules
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00965-2

Dhaneesh Kumar describes a method to enable the surface imaging of complex molecules.

title: Forty years of atomic force microscopy
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00953-6

Atomic force microscopy (AFM), first published in 1986, is now a workhorse of laboratories in physics and beyond. In this Viewpoint, seven scientists describe the variety of ways they use the technique and discuss how they’d like to see it develop in the future.

title: The physics of GaN-based light-emitting diodes
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00949-2

Because gallium nitride light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have made most of the visible spectrum available to LEDs, they have become the backbone of modern lighting applications. This Review examines three effects governing the physics of GaN-based LEDs: polarization fields, carrier localization and non-radiative defects.

title: How to probe lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00961-6

Furqanul Hassan Naqvi explains how careful Brillouin spectroscopy can provide insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.

title: The costs and benefits of physics research
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00958-1

Deciding what physics research to pursue involves cost–benefit analysis — which should include environmental impacts.

title: Atomic force microscopy from nanoscale imaging to holistic exploration
abstract:
Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s42254-026-00956-3

Forty years after its invention, atomic force microscopy has evolved from a simple surface imaging tool into one of the most versatile measurement platforms in nanoscience. This Comment traces the key innovations.
